learning: If line_loss_events reach 0 but max_error stays near 0.06 m, steering authority or lag is the limit, not coverage. If line losses persist at 20 mm, coverage is still the limit and the footprint should be tested next.
notes: Robot package for the 20 mm pitch test. The controller gains change slightly (kp 1.2 to 1.4, kd 0.1 to 0.15) to add steering authority, since iteration 1 showed steady drift with low oscillation and no max_error gain from narrowing the track.
rationale: Iteration 1 (entityR2B, score 53.3955) changed the sensor pitch from 10 mm to 15 mm and the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.066 m, line_loss_events stayed at 1 to 2 per run, and steering_oscillation stayed low at 0.07 to 0.16. All 60 trials still ended off_track. So the 15 mm bar did not close the coverage gap, and narrowing the track did not raise yaw authority enough to change max_error (oval 0.0608 to 0.0621). The robot drifts steadily at low oscillation, which points to too little corrective steering rather than jitter. Geometry follows the Builder's entity0 exactly: 20 mm pitch (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 at y = 0.04), 12 mm footprints, 0.12 m body width, 0.7 kg mass, 0.10 m track and 0.03 m wheels. Only the sensor pitch changes from iteration 1, so the pitch effect is isolated. Controller: I keep the sensor weights at [-2,-1,0,1,2] so the signal scale does not change. I raise kp from 1.2 to 1.4 to add steering authority, because the drift is steady and the oscillation evidence (max 0.16) leaves room. I raise kd from 0.1 to 0.15 to damp the extra gain. ki and base_speed stay the same, and line_loss stays last_direction so the line-recovery behaviour is unchanged. Expected: line_loss_events fall toward 0 with the wider bar. max_error may fall below 0.06 m if the extra kp helps; this is an assumption, not a measured result.
